in_hebrew.name: לוטית
in_hebrew.long_meaning: A derivative of the Hebrew word 'lutet' meaning 'lady' or 'woman'. It is not found in the Bible, but the root is present in several biblical names such as Leah (which means 'wild cow' or 'weary' but is derived from 'lutet'), and Lottie may have been used as a derivative of these names in non-biblical contexts.

in_greek.name: Λοττή
in_greek.long_meaning: A Greek name derived from the word 'lottos' meaning 'lot' or 'destiny'. It is not found in the Bible, but the root is present in several biblical names such as Lot, who was given the name by God due to his role in the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah.

in_latin.name: Lotia
in_latin.long_meaning: A Latin name derived from the word 'lactis' meaning 'milk'. It is not found in the Bible, but the root is present in several biblical names such as Lactantius, a Latin philosopher and early Christian apologist.
